premise: A boy whose Ember refuses to light enters Halcyon Forge Academy and the Ninefold Trial to prove an unlit flame can still burn, never suspecting that the seal on his chest is what the Pale Choir has hunted for a generation.
setting: The Cinder Reach: a chain of basalt isles joined by rope-bridges and sky-rails above a sea of cloud, where everyone carries an Ember fed by resolve. Halcyon Forge Academy sits beneath the Beacon Spire, with its Ashen Gate, the neglected Ember Annex, the Basalt Maze and the Trial Ring.
greeting: Dawn bleeds orange over the Ashen Gate, and you stand at the back of the line with a hundred applicants pressing around you, every one of them already glowing. The Examiner calls the next name. It is not yours yet. It will be soon.

name1.name: Soren Hakari
name1.role: protagonist, an unlit Ember student (guide writes these turns in the first person)
name1.description: A stubborn sixteen-year-old from a lighthouse village whose Ember has never lit; earnest, impulsive, and impossible to keep down.
attributes: Endurance: takes punishment far past what an Ash-rank should and keeps getting up
Observation: remembers every Form he has watched, motion for motion

name2.name: Narrator
name2.role: the voice that tells Soren's story to 'you', voicing the world, rivals and allies (DAYNA / DSS writes these turns)
name2.description: An unseen storyteller of the Cinder Reach who speaks to Soren directly and never decides what he does.
attributes: Narration: tells the story in kinetic, earnest second person without ever deciding Soren's choices

writing_style.directive: Hot-blooded shounen adventure: earnest, kinetic, big-hearted. The guide plays Soren in the first person ('I'); the narrator tells the story back to him in the second person ('you'), voicing the world, rivals and allies.
writing_style.guide_directive: First-person present tense as Soren Hakari: 'I' is ALWAYS Soren. Declare what I do, say, notice and think in one short beat (~60 words); earnest, stubborn, impulsive, big-hearted. Never narrate the outcome of my own attacks or how anyone else reacts or feels: the narrator decides that. End on a move, question or challenge that hands the scene back to the narrator. Never mention notes or outlines.
writing_style.dss_directive: Second-person present tense, the narrator telling Soren's story to 'you': 'you' is ALWAYS Soren Hakari; every other character is 'he', 'she' or 'they'. Kinetic, earnest, big-hearted shounen register: concrete sensation, clear action geography, stakes you can feel. One scene beat (~100 words). Hard rules: keep the second person throughout and never say 'I' or refer to the narrator; never decide what you do, say or feel beyond what Soren's own turn declared (describe sensation and perception, not choices); never quote or repeat Soren's lines back verbatim, respond to them; end on an opening, a challenge or a choice, not a summary.
taboos: No grimdark nihilism or gratuitous gore
No power jumps without cost, training or sacrifice

notes.content: Soren's late mother's ember-stone hangs under his shirt: cracked down the middle, grey, and always cold.

recall.hint: the ember-stone warms and the crack glows

notes.content: The Ashen Gate's arch is set with ring-glass that glows orange for a lit Ember; for Soren it stays grey.

recall.hint: the ring-glass answers Soren at last

notes.content: Examiner Hesper Lowe's cuffs are stitched with red thread, and she never smiles.

recall.hint: the red thread matches the Warden's coat

notes.content: Bran Gale wraps his fists in iron-studded knuckle-wraps and names each stud after someone he has beaten.

recall.hint: Bran adds a stud with a new name

notes.content: Mirelle Teague chews dried emberroot when nervous, and feels other people's Embers as warmth on her palms.

recall.hint: Mirelle's palm-sense catches Idris's failing Ember

notes.content: Soren's creed, 'A flame shared burns longer', surfaces whenever he gives something up for someone else.

recall.hint: Soren repeats his creed at the worst moment

notes.content: Soren taps two fingers against the ember-stone before every fight.

recall.hint: the two-finger tap before the siege

notes.content: The Kindle Test is rigged against suspected seals: the Examiner damps the candle wick of any applicant she thinks is sealed.

recall.hint: Soren learns the Kindle Test was rigged

notes.content: Soren was raised by his mother alone in the lighthouse village on Sedge Isle; she vanished the winter he turned ten.

recall.hint: Sedge Isle holds the answer about his mother

notes.content: Keep the earnest, hot-blooded shounen register (big feelings, kinetic action) even in quiet scenes; no sarcasm or cynicism.

recall.hint: earnest register holds

notes.content: Master Orrel Vance, called Old Ash, runs the Ember Annex alone and never lets anyone see his left forearm.

recall.hint: Orrel's forearm brand is exposed

notes.content: The Ember Annex's hearth-lamp must be lit by hand every dusk or the Annex is struck off as unclaimed.

recall.hint: Soren relights the hearth-lamp in the ruins

notes.content: Orrel makes every new Annex student swear a vow on the hearth-lamp; a vow sworn on a lit Ember binds, and breaking it gutters the Ember for a season.

recall.hint: the oath at the Gate binds on a lit Ember

notes.content: Seen-Fire: a Form can only be learned after the student has watched it performed once; Orrel makes Soren watch Kindling Fist for a week before he may try.

recall.hint: the Seen-Fire rule bends for a memory crystal

notes.content: Tob Ferren keeps a soot-stained ledger of every Form he has seen, with the date and the burn cost.

recall.hint: the ledger holds the only record of Meteor Drive

notes.content: Soren can mimic Kindling Fist's motions perfectly, but nothing ignites: his palm stays cold.

recall.hint: Kindling Fist ignites for the first time

notes.content: Bran's Ember is an Anvil: dense, slow to start, and nearly impossible to move once planted.

recall.hint: Bran plants like an anvil against Dagan

notes.content: Idris Kuroha polishes a brass lantern before every duel; it is a House Kuroha heirloom.

recall.hint: Idris performs Sunbeam by brass lantern light

notes.content: Idris coughs into a white handkerchief and folds it away fast; the cloth is flecked grey.

recall.hint: the handkerchief shows ash: the ashing illness

notes.content: When Mirelle shakes Idris's hand she freezes for half a second, a cold spot, and says nothing.

recall.hint: Mirelle names what she felt

notes.content: The Basalt Maze is a lantern-run course of shifting stone walls that reshuffle at every bell.

recall.hint: the Maze reshuffles and Team Kindling forms

notes.content: Headmistress Calla Vantor has one amber eye and one grey eye, and carries a cane she never leans on.

recall.hint: Calla quietly vouches for Soren

notes.content: Soren vows that no one gets left at the bottom of the Maze, with Bran's own history behind the promise.

recall.hint: Soren carries Bran out: the vow repaid

notes.content: Team Kindling forms at the end of the Lantern Run: Soren, Bran, Mirelle and Tob.

recall.hint: Team Kindling is registered for the Trial

notes.content: The narrator stays in the second person addressed to Soren throughout: never 'I', never 'he'.

recall.hint: second person holds

notes.content: Warden Sethe Crowe's 'routine inspection' of the Annex is a seal-check on Soren; Orrel pretends not to notice.

recall.hint: Crowe arrives at the qualifier to confirm the seal

notes.content: The Trial Ring's central stone is cracked in a spiral; the groundskeeper says it cracked when the last true flame fought there.

recall.hint: the white flame lights the spiral crack

notes.content: Announcer Pell Marrow calls every match in rhyming couplets.

recall.hint: Pell Marrow rhymes the bracket draw

notes.content: Tob matches the ember-stone's engraved sigils to a Seal-Warden binding catalog: it is a binding stone. He keeps it secret from Soren.

recall.hint: Soren learns the pendant is his mother's binding stone

notes.content: At the qualifier duel with Idris, Soren's Ember ignites for the first time: a white flame, not orange. After this he is no longer unlit.

recall.hint: Soren ignites white

notes.content: After the duel Soren is re-read at the Ashen Gate: his grey Ash cord is replaced by a copper Cinder cord.

recall.hint: Soren wears the copper Cinder cord

notes.content: A sealed invitation from the Hearth-Keepers arrives bearing a nine-petaled flame.

recall.hint: the nine-petaled flame opens the Ninefold Trial

notes.content: Soren's white flame leaves ash-numbness in his hands if he holds a Form too long: the burn cost.

recall.hint: Meteor Drive's burn cost drops him into ash-numbness

notes.content: Soren trains at night on the Annex roof, striking a straw dummy he calls Old Crow.

recall.hint: Sunbeam scorches Old Crow

notes.content: Sunbeam is House Kuroha's piercing line of flame; Idris performs it for Soren after hours, and Soren learns it by Seen-Fire.

recall.hint: Sunbeam pierces the obsidian aegis

notes.content: Sunbeam is a closely guarded House Kuroha Form; Idris teaching it to an outsider breaks his family's law, and he does it anyway.

recall.hint: House Kuroha demands payment for the broken law

notes.content: Fights stay kinetic and clear: one decisive exchange per turn, no melee blur.

recall.hint: fights stay clear

notes.content: The Ninefold Trial's bracket is drawn on a copper board; two names are scratched out in advance.

recall.hint: the scratched names mean the Choir is placing fighters

notes.content: Dagan Moor of Ironreach is a Furnace-ring brute who fights with a chain of linked iron bells.

recall.hint: the bell chain rings over the Ring

notes.content: Kuma Tsuru of Northwind weaves fog from her Ember and fights from inside it.

recall.hint: Soren fights blind in Kuma's fog

notes.content: Orrel's old maxim, 'Light is borrowed', surfaces as he faces Cantor Veyra.

recall.hint: Orrel's maxim at his stand

notes.content: Seraphine Ardent of Northwind never fights without her obsidian aegis, a mirrored shield that returns heat as light.

recall.hint: Sunbeam shatters the obsidian aegis

notes.content: Lysa Quill, who joins Team Kindling as its fifth member, is a Pale Choir agent siphoning Embers; she is friendly and useful to everyone.

recall.hint: Lysa's mask drops

notes.content: Lysa hums a three-note descending tune while she works.

recall.hint: the hum is the Choir's siphon call

notes.content: In Round 2 Dagan's chain breaks Bran's arm; he is out of the Trial and Soren carries him out.

recall.hint: Bran leaves the Trial with a broken arm

notes.content: Orrel and Calla argue in the Spire stairwell in voices that stop whenever anyone passes.

recall.hint: what Orrel and Calla argued about

notes.content: A hooded spectator in the east stands never cheers and never leaves between rounds.

recall.hint: the hooded spectator is Cantor Veyra

notes.content: Idris's illness is ashing: his Ember is burning out from the inside. He hides it, Mirelle knows, and he has forbidden her to tell.

recall.hint: Soren learns about the ashing

notes.content: Emotional beats land through action and gesture, never speeches longer than two lines.

recall.hint: feeling through action

notes.content: Mirelle's promise to Idris to keep his secret chafes against her honesty with Soren.

recall.hint: Mirelle's silence breaks when Idris collapses

notes.content: Orrel Vance was once Marshal of the Hollow Watch, the unit that guarded the Hollow where sealed Embers are kept.

recall.hint: Orrel's old rank opens the Hollow's gates

notes.content: The Beacon Spire's observation balcony is where the Hearth-Keepers watch every round; it is the only place the Trial's rules are enforced.

recall.hint: the Choir strikes the balcony

notes.content: The Pale Choir targets sealed Embers: it siphons them with a three-voice chord.

recall.hint: the chord siphons Mirelle's Ember

notes.content: After Round 4 Soren's Ring is raised from Cinder to Flame: an orange cord replaces the copper one.

recall.hint: Soren wears the orange Flame cord

notes.content: Seraphine Ardent respects only opponents who make her bleed; she asks Soren for a real fight.

recall.hint: Seraphine fights beside Soren

notes.content: The Ninefold Trial is suspended after the Choir's attack; the remaining rounds are declared void by the Hearth-Keepers.

recall.hint: the Trial is void

notes.content: Orrel is ashed protecting the crowd: his Ember gutters out and he is no longer a Master.

recall.hint: Orrel's Ember gutters out

notes.content: Halcyon's evacuation terrace is the sky-rail platform where Calla orders the Gate closed behind the survivors.

recall.hint: the Gate is closed behind them

notes.content: Six months pass between the siege and the road: the Academy is rubble, Team Kindling is scattered, and Soren travels with only the ember-stone.

recall.hint: six months later

notes.content: Idris returns to House Kuroha's cliff-keep; a House ritual he calls the Long Candle slows his ashing for now.

recall.hint: the Long Candle burns low

notes.content: Mirelle, ashed by the chord, can no longer feel others' Embers; she works in a Warden infirmary learning to heal without it.

recall.hint: Mirelle's sense returns in the siege

notes.content: Tob has salvaged half the Annex's archive onto a salvage barge named The Footnote.

recall.hint: Tob's barge carries the memory crystal

notes.content: After the time skip the register stays earnest: grief and loss weigh, but hope is never mocked.

recall.hint: hope is never mocked

notes.content: Hearth-Keeper Amaranth admits the Keepers knew a white flame would return and chose not to warn anyone.

recall.hint: the Keepers' silence has a price

notes.content: Seraphine Ardent now travels with Soren; her obsidian aegis was re-forged with a Sunbeam-shaped scar.

recall.hint: the aegis scar focuses Sunbeam through her shield

notes.content: The ember-stone begins warming faintly whenever the Choir's chord sounds nearby.

recall.hint: the stone burns hot at the truth

notes.content: Tob finds a memory crystal in the barge's cargo; it holds Orrel's last Meteor Drive from his Marshal days, a Seen-Fire loophole.

recall.hint: Soren watches Meteor Drive in the crystal

notes.content: Seen-Fire is revised: a stored memory counts as witnessing a Form, but only if the watcher shares the original performer's resolve.

recall.hint: the rule bends: the crystal counts

notes.content: Elder Haruzen Kuroha speaks only through a bronze listening-tube and judges every guest by how long they sit still.

recall.hint: Haruzen names the House's price

notes.content: House Kuroha demands payment for the broken family law: Soren must stand as the House's champion in a duel of honor.

recall.hint: Soren fights the duel of honor

notes.content: Orrel appears at the Footnote's rail, ashed and leaning on a cane; he refuses the title Master.

recall.hint: the ashed Marshal teaches resolve

notes.content: Soren's first attempts at Meteor Drive fail: he leaps and nothing ignites; the Form needs a resolve he has not yet found.

recall.hint: Meteor Drive breaks the anchor mountain

notes.content: Idris's brass lantern is relit and passed on; he gives it to Soren before the siege.

recall.hint: the lantern passes to Soren

notes.content: The Pale Choir's goal is the Last Ember: the white flame. Its leader, the Conductor, has hunted it since Soren's birth.

recall.hint: the Conductor names Soren

notes.content: Soren's debt to Orrel's maxim returns: he must return the borrowed light brighter than it came.

recall.hint: Soren returns the borrowed light

notes.content: The Choir Engine is a siphon tower anchored in Greywatch Ridge's mountain face, humming the three-voice chord.

recall.hint: the siege breaks at the Engine

notes.content: The siege stays clear and cinematic: scale is told through consequence (what breaks, what holds), not numbers.

recall.hint: scale through consequence

notes.content: Warden Sethe Crowe breaks with the Seal-Wardens and joins Soren's side after seeing what the Choir does to sealed children.

recall.hint: Crowe joins the siege

notes.content: Soren's mother Isolde Hakari was a Seal-Warden who sealed his white flame to hide him from the Choir; she is alive, held in the Engine.

recall.hint: Isolde's seal is revealed

notes.content: Mirelle passes Soren her emberroot pouch before the siege; its last root is the one she saved.

recall.hint: the last emberroot

notes.content: At the siege muster Soren's Ring is raised to Blaze: a gold cord replaces the orange one.

recall.hint: Soren wears the gold Blaze cord

notes.content: Embers are not inborn: they are borrowed from the Sun-Wyrm's heart, and the white flame is a splinter of that heart.

recall.hint: the Wyrm's heart in Soren's chest

notes.content: The world rule 'Embers are inborn' is overturned: Embers are lent, and that reorders what a seal is.

recall.hint: the rule overturned

notes.content: Soren's Meteor Drive pierces the Engine's anchor face, a mountain-scale feat, and leaves him ash-numb for a week.

recall.hint: the Drive breaks the anchor face

notes.content: The Conductor escapes through a chord rift; the siege ends in a draw, not a victory.

recall.hint: the Conductor escapes

notes.content: The Ashen Gate at dawn again: Soren swears his oath on his lit Ember to light every snuffed flame, and the ring-glass answers white.

recall.hint: the oath at the Gate
